subproblems.title: The divergence of a C¹ field compactly supported in the open unit cube integrates to zero over the cube
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1 and Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure). If g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ is C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1), has compact support and tsupport g ⊆ Q₁, then ∫_{Q₁} div g = 0, where div g(y) := trace Dg(y) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv ℝ g y).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 of the parent proof (the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cube_bv_median): "for every constant β and admissible g, ∫_{Q₁} β div g = 0 (integrate each ∂_i g_i along coordinate lines; g has compact support in Q₁)". It is proved here for C¹ fields; the line integration is written as an integration by parts on ℝⁿ, and the coordinate-line version is given as an alternative in step 2. In Simon this is the fact, implicit in displays (29)–(30) of the proof of Ch. 6, 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1862–1876), that subtracting the constant multiple β[[F]] does not change the boundary inside F̊.

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate and e_1, …, e_n is the standard orthonormal basis. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv ℝ G x, viewed as a linear map). For v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ‖Dv(x)‖ is the operator norm of fderiv ℝ v x, which equals the Euclidean length |∇v(x)| of the gradient. Integrals over a set are Bochner integrals for the restricted Lebesgue measure. Under the measure-preserving, coordinate-preserving continuous linear equivalence WithLp.ofLp : Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp / EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp; it is not an isometry for the sup norm of Fin n → ℝ, and no isometry property is used) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ); hence vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded, and Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁ for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let g be C¹ with compact support, and put K := tsupport g, a compact subset of Q₁.

1. Regularity. Dg : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) is continuous because g is C¹. Moreover Dg(x) = 0 for x ∉ K: such an x has the open neighbourhood ℝⁿ ∖ K on which g ≡ 0 (Mathlib support_fderiv_subset: support (fderiv ℝ g) ⊆ tsupport g). Hence for each fixed h ∈ ℝⁿ the map x ↦ Dg(x)h is continuous with support in the compact set K, so it is integrable on ℝⁿ; likewise g is continuous with compact support, hence integrable. The map A ↦ trace A is linear on the finite-dimensional space L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), hence continuous, so x ↦ div g(x) is continuous, vanishes outside K and is integrable on ℝⁿ.

2. Directional derivatives integrate to zero. Fix h ∈ ℝⁿ. Apply integration by parts on ℝⁿ (Mathlib integral_smul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_smul_of_integrable, Lebesgue measure on Euclid n) to the scalar function f ≡ 1 and the vector function g in the direction h. Its hypotheses hold: x ↦ Df(x)h • g(x) = 0 is integrable; x ↦ f(x) • Dg(x)h = Dg(x)h is integrable by step 1; x ↦ f(x) • g(x) = g(x) is integrable by step 1; f is differentiable everywhere; g is differentiable everywhere (C¹). It gives ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)h dx = −∫_{ℝⁿ} Df(x)h • g(x) dx = −∫ 0 = 0. Import note: this lemma lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts, which is not in the import closure of the frozen GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean; add `import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts` to Submission.lean. Adding Mathlib imports to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean is accepted practice in this run (29 accepted nodes do so, e.g. 10 import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense and 10 import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.SmoothApprox); the challenge and the solution of the child comparator both import the candidate Submission, so the frozen type is unaffected. Alternative route inside the closure, needed only for h = e_i in step 3: identify Euclid n with Fin n → ℝ (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) and split off coordinate i (MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove, x = Fin.insertNth i t x'); by Fubini ∫_{ℝⁿ} ∂_i g_k = ∫_{x'} (∫_ℝ (d/dt) g_k(Fin.insertNth i t x') dt) dx', and for each x' the inner integral vanishes by MeasureTheory.integral_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrable (t ↦ g_k(Fin.insertNth i t x') is C¹ with compact support, so it and its derivative are integrable on ℝ).

3. Trace in the standard basis. For every linear T : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, trace T = Σ_i ⟨e_i, T e_i⟩ (Mathlib LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner with the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun). Hence div g(x) = Σ_i ⟨e_i, Dg(x)e_i⟩ for every x. Since v ↦ ⟨e_i, v⟩ is a continuous linear functional and x ↦ Dg(x)e_i is integrable, ∫_{ℝⁿ} ⟨e_i, Dg(x)e_i⟩ dx = ⟨e_i, ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)e_i dx⟩ = ⟨e_i, 0⟩ = 0 by step 2 (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm for innerSL ℝ e_i). Summing over i (integral of a finite sum of integrable functions): ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g = 0.

4. Restriction to Q₁. By step 1, div g vanishes outside K ⊆ Q₁, so ∫_{Q₁} div g = ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, applied to the integrand that vanishes off Q₁). By step 3 this is 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Dg is continuous and vanishes off tsupport g ⊆ Q₁, so g, every Dg(·)h and div g are integrable on ℝⁿ.
Integration by parts against the constant function 1 (or FTC along coordinate lines) gives ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)h dx = 0 for every direction h.
div g = Σ_i ⟨e_i, Dg e_i⟩, so ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g = Σ_i ⟨e_i, ∫ Dg e_i⟩ = 0.
div g vanishes off Q₁, so ∫_{Q₁} div g = ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g = 0.

Fix u, V with u integrable on Q₁ and hyp(u, V), and fix δ > 0.

0. V ≥ 0: the map g ≡ 0 is C^∞, has compact support, tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ Q₁ and |0| ≤ 1; D0 = 0 and trace 0 = 0, so hyp gives 0 = ∫_{Q₁} u · 0 ≤ V.

1. Mollifier. For σ > 0 fix φ_σ : ℝⁿ → ℝ, C^∞, φ_σ ≥ 0, ∫φ_σ = 1, with support in the open ball B_σ(0) := {|z| < σ} (e.g. the normalized Mathlib bump (ContDiffBump with rIn = σ/2, rOut = σ).normed volume, or φ_σ(z) := σ^{−n}φ(z/σ) for a fixed such φ with support in B_1(0)). Then A_σ := sup_z ‖Dφ_σ(z)‖ < ∞ (Dφ_σ is continuous with compact support). Let ū := 1_{Q₁}u, which is integrable on ℝⁿ, and u_σ(x) := ∫ ū(y) φ_σ(x − y) dy (the convolution ū ⋆ φ_σ, Mathlib convolution with L = ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ).

2. Smoothness and derivative of u_σ. Since φ_σ is C^∞ with compact support and ū is locally integrable, u_σ is C^∞ and Du_σ(x)h = ∫ ū(y) Dφ_σ(x − y)h dy for all x, h (differentiation under the integral sign; Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right and HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right, followed by applying the continuous linear map to h). Then g is Borel measurable, |g| ≤ 1, g = 0 off Q_δ (so g is integrable on ℝⁿ), and Du_σ(x)(g(x)) = 1_{Q_δ}(x)‖Du_σ(x)‖ for every x.
 (b) Define g̃(y) := ∫ φ_σ(x − y) g(x) dx. With φ̌_σ(z) := φ_σ(−z) (C^∞, compact support) this is the convolution g̃(y) = ∫ φ̌_σ(y − x) g(x) dx = (φ̌_σ ⋆ g)(y). (i) g̃ is C^∞ and Dg̃(y)h = ∫ (Dφ̌_σ(y − x)h) g(x) dx = −∫ (Dφ_σ(x − y)h) g(x) dx (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left with n = ⊤, giving exactly ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞), and HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left; chain rule Dφ̌_σ(z) = −Dφ_σ(−z)). Taking the trace in the standard orthonormal basis (trace T = Σ_j ⟨e_j, T e_j⟩): div g̃(y) = −∫ Σ_j (Dφ_σ(x − y)e_j) g_j(x) dx = −∫ Dφ_σ(x − y)(g(x)) dx. (ii) |g̃(y)| ≤ ∫ φ_σ(x − y)|g(x)| dx ≤ ∫ φ_σ = 1. (iii) If g̃(y) ≠ 0 there is x ∈ Q_δ with φ_σ(x − y) ≠ 0, i.e. |x − y| < σ; then |x_i − y_i| < σ, so δ − σ < y_i < 1 − δ + σ for all i. Hence tsupport g̃ ⊆ P := {y : δ − σ ≤ y_i ≤ 1 − δ + σ for all i}, a closed bounded (hence compact) set with P ⊆ Q₁ because 0 < δ − σ and 1 − δ + σ < 1. So g̃ has compact support and tsupport g̃ ⊆ Q₁. The same holds for −g̃, and D(−g̃) = −Dg̃, div(−g̃) = −div g̃.
 (c) Applying hyp(u, V) to −g̃: −∫_{Q₁} u · div g̃ = ∫_{Q₁} u · div(−g̃) ≤ V.
 (d) Identity. The function (x, y) ↦ ū(y) Dφ_σ(x − y)(g(x)) is a.e.-strongly measurable on ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ and bounded in absolute value by A_σ|ū(y)|1_{Q_δ}(x), which is integrable on ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ (its integral is A_σ‖ū‖₁ vol(Q_δ) < ∞). By step 2 and Fubini, ∫_{ℝⁿ} Du_σ(x)(g(x)) dx = ∫_x ∫_y ū(y) Dφ_σ(x − y)(g(x)) dy dx = ∫_y ū(y)(∫_x Dφ_σ(x − y)(g(x)) dx) dy = ∫_y ū(y)(−div g̃(y)) dy = −∫_{Q₁} u · div g̃, by (b)(i) and ū = 1_{Q₁}u.
 (e) By (a), (d), (c): ∫_{Q_δ}‖Du_σ‖ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} Du_σ(x)(g(x)) dx = −∫_{Q₁} u · div g̃ ≤ V. (If δ ≥ 1/2 then Q_δ = ∅, g = g̃ = 0, and the bound reads 0 ≤ V, which is step 0.)

4. L¹ convergence: ∫_{ℝⁿ}|u_σ − ū| → 0 as σ → 0⁺.
 (a) L¹ contraction. For f integrable on ℝⁿ and f_σ := f ⋆ φ_σ, Tonelli and ∫φ_σ = 1 give ∫|f_σ| ≤ ∫∫|f(y)|φ_σ(x − y) dy dx = ∫|f|. By linearity of convolution, ∫|u_σ − h_σ| ≤ ∫|ū − h| for every integrable h, where h_σ := h ⋆ φ_σ.
 (b) Continuous compactly supported h. Let h be continuous with compact support S. Then h is uniformly continuous; put ω(σ) := sup{|h(x − z) − h(x)| : x ∈ ℝⁿ, |z| ≤ σ}, so ω(σ) → 0 as σ → 0. Since h_σ(x) − h(x) = ∫ φ_σ(z)(h(x − z) − h(x)) dz, |h_σ(x) − h(x)| ≤ ω(σ) for all x. (Mathlib ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le states this bound for the convolution with the normed bump on the left, (φ.normed ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ] h)(x); it equals h_σ(x) = (h ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ] φ_σ)(x) by commutativity of convolution, Mathlib convolution_flip, because (lsmul ℝ ℝ).flip = lsmul ℝ ℝ on ℝ × ℝ. Alternatively use the displayed estimate directly.) For σ ≤ 1, h_σ − h vanishes outside the compact set S₁ := {x : dist(x, S) ≤ 1}. Hence ∫|h_σ − h| ≤ vol(S₁)ω(σ) → 0.
 (c) Given ε > 0 choose h continuous with compact support and ∫|ū − h| < ε (density; Mathlib Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le). Then ∫|u_σ − ū| ≤ ∫|u_σ − h_σ| + ∫|h_σ − h| + ∫|h − ū| ≤ 2ε + ∫|h_σ − h|, so limsup_{σ→0⁺}∫|u_σ − ū| ≤ 2ε. As ε > 0 is arbitrary, ∫|u_σ − ū| → 0.

5. Conclusion. Put σ_k := δ/(k + 2) (so 0 < σ_k < δ and σ_k → 0) and v_k := u_{σ_k}. By step 2 each v_k is C^∞, in particular C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1). By step 3, ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ ≤ V for every k. Since Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ and ū = u on Q₁, and v_k is bounded while u is integrable on Q_δ (so v_k − u is integrable on Q_δ), 0 ≤ ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| = ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − ū| ≤ ∫_{ℝⁿ}|u_{σ_k} − ū| → 0 by step 4. Hence ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| → 0 as k → ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: V ≥ 0 from the test field g ≡ 0.
u_σ := (1_{Q₁}u) ⋆ φ_σ is C^∞ with Du_σ(x)h = ∫ ū(y) Dφ_σ(x − y)h dy.
For σ < δ, with g := 1_{Q_δ}∇u_σ/|∇u_σ| and g̃ := φ̌_σ ⋆ g (C^∞, |g̃| ≤ 1, tsupport in a compact subset of Q₁), Fubini gives ∫_{Q_δ}‖Du_σ‖ = −∫_{Q₁} u div g̃ ≤ V (hyp applied to −g̃).
u_σ → 1_{Q₁}u in L¹(ℝⁿ) by the L¹ contraction plus density of continuous compactly supported functions.
v_k := u_{δ/(k+2)} are C¹, satisfy the gradient bound and converge to u in L¹(Q_δ).

subproblems.title: Poincaré inequality on the cube Q_δ for C¹ functions, double-integral form
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, δ ≥ 0 and Q_δ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure). For every C¹ function v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ∫_{x ∈ Q_δ} ∫_{y ∈ Q_δ} |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ 2ⁿ√n ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Dv‖, where 2ⁿ√n = 2^{m+1}√(m + 1) and ‖Dv(x)‖ is the operator norm of fderiv ℝ v x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (v : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (δ : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 v → 0 ≤ δ → ∫ x in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ∫ y in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, |v x - v y| ≤ 2 ^ (m + 1) * Real.sqrt (m + 1) * ∫ x in {z : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < z i ∧ z i < 1 - δ}, ‖fderiv ℝ v x‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cube_bv_median: smooth Poincaré inequality on a cube of side s ≤ 1), stopped at its intermediate double-integral bound ∫∫|v(x) − v(y)| dx dy ≤ √n s·2ⁿsⁿ∫|∇v| and specialized to the cube Q' = Q_δ (any δ ≥ 0, so any side s = 1 − 2δ ≤ 1). In Simon this is the "usual Poincaré inequality for smooth functions" invoked in the proof of Ch. 2, 2.7 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 651–658).

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate and e_1, …, e_n is the standard orthonormal basis. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv ℝ G x, viewed as a linear map). For v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ‖Dv(x)‖ is the operator norm of fderiv ℝ v x, which equals the Euclidean length |∇v(x)| of the gradient. Integrals over a set are Bochner integrals for the restricted Lebesgue measure. Under the measure-preserving, coordinate-preserving continuous linear equivalence WithLp.ofLp : Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp / EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp; it is not an isometry for the sup norm of Fin n → ℝ, and no isometry property is used) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ); hence vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded, and Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁ for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let v be C¹ and δ ≥ 0. Write Q := Q_δ, s := 1 − 2δ ≤ 1 and F(x) := ‖Dv(x)‖ ≥ 0, a continuous function.

0. Trivial case and finiteness. If s ≤ 0 then Q = ∅ and both sides are 0. Assume 0 < s ≤ 1. Then vol(Q) = sⁿ, Q is convex, and |x − y| ≤ √n s for x, y ∈ Q (each |x_i − y_i| < s). v and F are continuous, hence bounded on the compact closure of Q; so all integrands below are bounded measurable functions on sets of finite measure, every integral is finite, the iterated Bochner integral on the left equals the iterated Lebesgue integral of the nonnegative function |v(x) − v(y)|, and Tonelli's theorem applies to the nonnegative continuous integrands below.

1. Segment estimate. For x, y ∈ Q, γ(t) := v((1 − t)x + ty) is C¹ on [0, 1] with γ'(t) = Dv((1 − t)x + ty)(y − x). By the fundamental theorem of calculus, |v(y) − v(x)| = |∫_0^1 γ'(t) dt| ≤ ∫_0^1 F((1 − t)x + ty)|y − x| dt ≤ √n s ∫_0^1 F((1 − t)x + ty) dt.

2. Integrating over Q × Q and using Tonelli for (x, y, t) ↦ F((1 − t)x + ty) ≥ 0 on Q × Q × [0, 1]: ∫_Q ∫_Q |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ √n s ∫_0^1 J(t) dt, where J(t) := ∫_Q ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + ty) dy dx.

3. Bound for t ∈ [1/2, 1]. Fix x ∈ Q. The map y ↦ (1 − t)x + ty is a translate of the dilation by t, whose Jacobian determinant is tⁿ; by the change-of-variables formula for dilations and translations of Lebesgue measure (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.setIntegral_comp_smul_of_pos for the dilation by t, and translation invariance of Lebesgue measure for the translation by (1 − t)x, e.g. MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb for the measure-preserving translation z ↦ (1 − t)x + z, or MeasureTheory.integral_add_left_eq_self applied to the integrand extended by zero outside the set; all integrands are bounded measurable on bounded sets, so the Bochner versions apply), ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + ty) dy = t^{−n} ∫_{(1 − t)x + tQ} F(z) dz. By convexity (1 − t)x + tQ ⊆ Q, and F ≥ 0, so this is ≤ t^{−n} ∫_Q F ≤ 2ⁿ ∫_Q F. Integrating over x ∈ Q (measure sⁿ): J(t) ≤ 2ⁿsⁿ ∫_Q F.

4. Bound for t ∈ [0, 1/2). By Tonelli, J(t) = ∫_Q ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + ty) dx dy. Fix y ∈ Q; the map x ↦ (1 − t)x + ty has Jacobian (1 − t)ⁿ ≥ 2^{−n} and maps Q into Q (convexity); as in step 3, ∫_Q F((1 − t)x + ty) dx ≤ (1 − t)^{−n} ∫_Q F ≤ 2ⁿ ∫_Q F, and integrating over y ∈ Q gives J(t) ≤ 2ⁿsⁿ ∫_Q F.

5. Conclusion. By steps 2–4, ∫_Q ∫_Q |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ √n s · 2ⁿsⁿ ∫_Q F = 2ⁿ√n s^{n+1} ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ ≤ 2ⁿ√n ∫_Q ‖Dv‖, because 0 < s ≤ 1 and ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ ≥ 0. With n = m + 1 this is 2^{m+1}√(m + 1) ∫_{Q_δ} ‖Dv‖. ∎
proof_key_steps: If δ ≥ 1/2 the cube is empty; otherwise s = 1 − 2δ ∈ (0, 1], vol(Q_δ) = sⁿ and |x − y| ≤ √n s on Q_δ.
FTC on segments: |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ √n s ∫_0^1 ‖Dv((1 − t)x + ty)‖ dt.
Tonelli and the affine change of variables (Jacobian tⁿ or (1 − t)ⁿ ≥ 2^{−n}, image in Q_δ by convexity) give J(t) ≤ 2ⁿsⁿ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv‖.
Hence ∫∫|v(x) − v(y)| ≤ 2ⁿ√n s^{n+1}∫‖Dv‖ ≤ 2ⁿ√n∫‖Dv‖.

subproblems.title: Poincaré inequality on the unit cube for functions of variation at most V
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure), div g := trace Dg. If u : ℝⁿ → ℝ is integrable on Q₁ and V ∈ ℝ satisfies ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1, then there is c ∈ ℝ with ∫_{Q₁} |u − c| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V = 2^{m+2}√(m + 1) V.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (V : ℝ), IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, u y * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g y) ≤ V) → ∃ c : ℝ, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - c| ≤ 2 ^ (m + 2) * Real.sqrt (m + 1) * V
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cube_bv_median: Poincaré inequality ∫_{Q₁}|u − u_{Q₁}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√nV via the limits σ ↓ 0, δ ↓ 0). Departure (a simplification): the limits are run on the double integral of step 2 instead of on the means over Q_δ, so no convergence of means is needed; the final c is the mean u_{Q₁} = ∫_{Q₁}u, as in the parent proof. In Simon this is the BV Poincaré inequality Ch. 2, 2.7 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 627–661) as used for the first line of display (32) in the proof of Ch. 6, 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1883–1892).

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate and e_1, …, e_n is the standard orthonormal basis. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv ℝ G x, viewed as a linear map). For v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ‖Dv(x)‖ is the operator norm of fderiv ℝ v x, which equals the Euclidean length |∇v(x)| of the gradient. Integrals over a set are Bochner integrals for the restricted Lebesgue measure. Under the measure-preserving, coordinate-preserving continuous linear equivalence WithLp.ofLp : Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp / EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp; it is not an isometry for the sup norm of Fin n → ℝ, and no isometry property is used) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ); hence vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded, and Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁ for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Sibling results used. smooth_approx (dimred_mbl_dt_cbm_smooth_approx): for u integrable on Q₁ with hyp(u, V) and δ > 0 there are C¹ functions v_k with ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ ≤ V for all k and ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| → 0. smooth_poincare (dimred_mbl_dt_cbm_smooth_poincare): for C¹ v and δ ≥ 0, ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ K₀∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv‖ with K₀ := 2ⁿ√n = 2^{m+1}√(m + 1).

Fix u integrable on Q₁ and V with hyp(u, V).

0. V ≥ 0: apply hyp to g ≡ 0 (C^∞, compact support, tsupport ∅ ⊆ Q₁, |0| ≤ 1; D0 = 0, trace 0 = 0): 0 = ∫_{Q₁} u · 0 ≤ V.

1. Finiteness. Since u is integrable on Q₁ and vol(Q₁) = 1 < ∞, the function (x, y) ↦ |u(x) − u(y)| ≤ |u(x)| + |u(y)| is integrable on Q₁ × Q₁ (product of the restricted measures; it is a.e.-strongly measurable as a composition of the a.e.-strongly measurable functions (x, y) ↦ u(x) and (x, y) ↦ u(y)). For every x and every δ ≥ 0 the function y ↦ |u(x) − u(y)| is integrable on Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ (u is integrable there and constants are integrable on sets of finite measure), so h_δ(x) := ∫_{Q_δ}|u(x) − u(y)| dy is finite, 0 ≤ h_δ(x) ≤ |u(x)| + ∫_{Q₁}|u|, and by Fubini x ↦ h_δ(x) is a.e.-strongly measurable on Q₁; hence h_δ is integrable on Q₁. Put D(δ) := ∫_{Q_δ} h_δ(x) dx = ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx.

2. D(δ) ≤ K₀V for every δ ∈ (0, 1/2). Fix such δ and take v_k from smooth_approx (δ > 0). Each v_k is continuous, hence bounded on the bounded set Q_δ, say |v_k| ≤ B_k there; so v_k − u is integrable on Q_δ and ε_k := ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| → 0. The function (x, y) ↦ |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| is continuous, hence measurable, and bounded by 2B_k on Q_δ × Q_δ; so d_k(x) := ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k(x) − v_k(y)| dy satisfies 0 ≤ d_k ≤ 2B_k vol(Q_δ) and is a.e.-strongly measurable (Fubini, Mathlib MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right'), hence integrable on Q_δ. By smooth_poincare (δ ≥ 0), D_k := ∫_{Q_δ} d_k = ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|v_k(x) − v_k(y)| dy dx ≤ K₀∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ ≤ K₀V. For all x, y: |u(x) − u(y)| ≤ |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| + |u(x) − v_k(x)| + |v_k(y) − u(y)|. For fixed x, integrating in y over Q_δ (all three terms are integrable in y) gives h_δ(x) ≤ d_k(x) + vol(Q_δ)|u(x) − v_k(x)| + ε_k. The three functions of x on the right are integrable on Q_δ (d_k as just shown, |u − v_k| because v_k − u is integrable on Q_δ, and the constant ε_k because vol(Q_δ) < ∞), and h_δ is integrable on Q_δ by step 1; integrating in x over Q_δ and using vol(Q_δ) ≤ 1: D(δ) ≤ D_k + vol(Q_δ)ε_k + vol(Q_δ)ε_k ≤ K₀V + 2ε_k. Letting k → ∞ gives D(δ) ≤ K₀V.

3. D(0) ≤ K₀V. Let δ_j := 1/(j + 3) for j ∈ ℕ; then δ_j ∈ (0, 1/2), δ_j ↓ 0, and every x ∈ Q₁ lies in Q_{δ_j} for all large j. For x ∈ Q₁, 1_{Q_{δ_j}}(y)|u(x) − u(y)| → 1_{Q₁}(y)|u(x) − u(y)| for every y ∈ Q₁, dominated by |u(x) − u(y)|, which is integrable in y over Q₁ for every x (step 1); so by dominated convergence h_{δ_j}(x) → h_0(x) for every x ∈ Q₁. Moreover 0 ≤ 1_{Q_{δ_j}}(x)h_{δ_j}(x) ≤ h_0(x) with h_0 integrable on Q₁, and 1_{Q_{δ_j}}(x)h_{δ_j}(x) → h_0(x) for every x ∈ Q₁. By dominated convergence D(δ_j) = ∫_{Q₁}1_{Q_{δ_j}}h_{δ_j} → ∫_{Q₁}h_0 = D(0). Since D(δ_j) ≤ K₀V for all j by step 2, D(0) ≤ K₀V.

4. Choice of c. Let c := ∫_{Q₁}u. Since vol(Q₁) = 1, for every x: u(x) − c = ∫_{Q₁}(u(x) − u(y)) dy, hence |u(x) − c| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u(x) − u(y)| dy = h_0(x). Integrating over Q₁ (both sides integrable): ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| ≤ D(0) ≤ K₀V = 2ⁿ√nV ≤ 2^{n+1}√nV, the last step because V ≥ 0 (step 0). With n = m + 1, 2^{n+1}√n = 2^{m+2}√(m + 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: V ≥ 0 from g ≡ 0; |u(x) − u(y)| is integrable on Q₁ × Q₁, so D(δ) := ∫_{Q_δ}∫_{Q_δ}|u(x) − u(y)| is finite.
For δ ∈ (0, 1/2): smooth_approx gives v_k, smooth_poincare gives D_k ≤ 2ⁿ√nV, and D(δ) ≤ D_k + 2∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u|; letting k → ∞, D(δ) ≤ 2ⁿ√nV.
δ_j = 1/(j + 3) ↓ 0 and dominated convergence give D(0) = ∫_{Q₁}∫_{Q₁}|u(x) − u(y)| ≤ 2ⁿ√nV.
With c = ∫_{Q₁}u (vol Q₁ = 1), ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| ≤ D(0) ≤ 2ⁿ√nV ≤ 2^{n+1}√nV.

subproblems.title: Integer median on the unit cube: it minimizes the L¹ deviation and is bounded by twice the L¹ norm
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure). If u : ℝⁿ → ℝ takes only integer values (u(y) ∈ ℤ for every y) and is integrable on Q₁, then there is β ∈ ℤ with ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| for every c ∈ ℝ and |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, u y = z) → IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → ∃ β : ℤ, (∀ c : ℝ, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - β| ≤ ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - c|) ∧ |(β : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y|

Source: step 4 (parent C2) of the parent proof (the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cube_bv_median: the least integer β with Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) ≥ 1/2 is a median; (a) a median minimizes c ↦ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c|; (b) |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|). In Simon these are the integer median choice (31) and the bound (35) in the proof of Ch. 6, 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1879–1883 and 1906–1908), whose minimizing property replaces the median hypothesis 2.7(‡) of Ch. 2.

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate and e_1, …, e_n is the standard orthonormal basis. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv ℝ G x, viewed as a linear map). For v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ‖Dv(x)‖ is the operator norm of fderiv ℝ v x, which equals the Euclidean length |∇v(x)| of the gradient. Integrals over a set are Bochner integrals for the restricted Lebesgue measure. Under the measure-preserving, coordinate-preserving continuous linear equivalence WithLp.ofLp : Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp / EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp; it is not an isometry for the sup norm of Fin n → ℝ, and no isometry property is used) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ); hence vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded, and Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁ for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let u be integer-valued and integrable on Q₁. Write μ for Lebesgue measure restricted to Q₁; μ(ℝⁿ) = vol(Q₁) = 1, and μ{P} denotes μ{y : P(y)}.

0. Measurability. u is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ, so there is a Borel function u' with u = u' μ-a.e.; hence each set {u ≤ c}, {u < c}, {u ≥ c}, {u > c} is μ-null-measurable and has the same μ-measure as the corresponding set for u' (equivalently, replace u' by the integer-valued Borel function round ∘ u', which equals u μ-a.e. because round(u(y)) = u(y)). All quantities in the statement (∫_{Q₁}|u − β|, ∫_{Q₁}|u − c|, ∫_{Q₁}|u|) are integrals of μ-integrable functions (μ is finite and u is μ-integrable), and they are unchanged under μ-a.e. modification; the pointwise inequalities below hold μ-a.e.

1. Distribution function. F(c) := μ{u ≤ c} is nondecreasing in c. As k → ∞ through ℕ, {u ≤ k} increases to ℝⁿ (u is real-valued), so F(k) → μ(ℝⁿ) = 1 by continuity from below; and {u ≤ −k} decreases to ∅, so F(−k) → 0 by continuity from above (μ is finite). Hence S := {k ∈ ℤ : F(k) ≥ 1/2} is nonempty (it contains large k) and bounded below (choose K with F(−K) < 1/2; then F(k) ≤ F(−K) < 1/2 for every integer k ≤ −K, so S ⊆ (−K, ∞)). Let β := min S (Mathlib Int.exists_least_of_bdd).

2. Median properties. F(β) = μ{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2 and F(β − 1) < 1/2. Since u is integer-valued, {u > β − 1} = {u ≥ β}, so μ{u ≥ β} = 1 − F(β − 1) > 1/2. Consequently μ{u > β} = 1 − μ{u ≤ β} ≤ 1/2 and μ{u < β} = 1 − μ{u ≥ β} < 1/2.

3. Minimality: ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| for every c ∈ ℝ.
 Case c ≥ β. Pointwise, on {u ≤ β} we have u ≤ β ≤ c, so |u − c| − |u − β| = (c − u) − (β − u) = c − β; on {u > β}, |u − c| − |u − β| ≥ −|c − β| = −(c − β) by the triangle inequality. Integrating over Q₁: ∫|u − c| − ∫|u − β| ≥ (c − β)(μ{u ≤ β} − μ{u > β}) ≥ (c − β)(1/2 − 1/2) = 0.
 Case c < β. On {u ≥ β}, |u − c| − |u − β| = (u − c) − (u − β) = β − c; on {u < β}, |u − c| − |u − β| ≥ −(β − c). Integrating: ∫|u − c| − ∫|u − β| ≥ (β − c)(μ{u ≥ β} − μ{u < β}) ≥ (β − c)(1/2 − 1/2) = 0.

4. Size of β. If β > 0: on {u ≥ β}, |u| ≥ u ≥ β, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ βμ{u ≥ β} ≥ β/2. If β < 0: on {u ≤ β}, |u| ≥ −u ≥ −β = |β|, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ |β|μ{u ≤ β} ≥ |β|/2. If β = 0 the claim is trivial since ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ 0. Hence |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|. ∎
proof_key_steps: Work μ-a.e. with a Borel representative (u = u' a.e., round ∘ u' integer-valued); vol(Q₁) = 1.
β := least integer k with vol(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ k}) ≥ 1/2 exists by continuity of the distribution function from below and above.
Integer values give vol{u ≥ β} > 1/2 and vol{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2, so β is a median.
A median minimizes c ↦ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| (pointwise comparison on {u ≤ β}, {u > β}, respectively {u ≥ β}, {u < β}).
|u| ≥ |β| on a set of measure ≥ 1/2, so |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.

subproblems.title: Divergence theorem with trace estimate on Q_δ for C¹ functions (0 ≤ δ ≤ 1/4)

Source: step 5 of the parent proof (the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cube_bv_median: divergence theorem on the box Q_δ for the field w_σG and the face (trace) inequality ∫_face|w_σ| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|w_σ| + ∫_{Q_δ}|∇w_σ| on each of the 2n faces), applied to an arbitrary C¹ function v in place of the mollified w_σ and for 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1/4 (side s = 1 − 2δ ∈ [1/2, 1], as in the parent's averaging step "length s ≥ 1/2"). ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate and e_1, …, e_n is the standard orthonormal basis. For v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ‖Dv(x)‖ is the operator norm of fderiv ℝ v x, which equals the Euclidean length |∇v(x)| of the gradient. Under the measure-preserving, coordinate-preserving continuous linear equivalence WithLp.ofLp : Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp / EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp; it is not an isometry for the sup norm of Fin n → ℝ, and no isometry property is used) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ); hence vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded, and Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁ for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let v, G be C¹ with |G| ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1/4. Put a := δ, b := 1 − δ, s := b − a = 1 − 2δ ∈ [1/2, 1], Q := Q_δ = (a, b)ⁿ, Q̄ := [a, b]ⁿ (compact). Write ∂_i v(x) := Dv(x)e_i and G_i := ⟨e_i, G⟩. For i ∈ {1, …, n}, t ∈ ℝ and x' ∈ ℝ^{n−1} let ι_i(t, x') ∈ ℝⁿ be the point whose i-th coordinate is t and whose other coordinates are x' in order (Mathlib Fin.insertNth); put Q' := (a, b)^{n−1} (for n = 1, ℝ⁰ is a point of measure 1, so the face integrals below are point evaluations).

Facts. (F1) div G(x) = trace DG(x) = Σ_i ⟨e_i, DG(x)e_i⟩ = Σ_i ∂_iG_i(x) (Mathlib LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner with EuclideanSpace.basisFun). (F2) Fubini in coordinate i: the map (t, x') ↦ ι_i(t, x') is a measure-preserving bijection ℝ × ℝ^{n−1} → ℝⁿ (Mathlib MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove composed with the measure-preserving identification Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ)) mapping (a, b) × Q' onto Q; hence ∫_Q h = ∫_{Q'} ∫_a^b h(ι_i(t, x')) dt dx' for every h integrable on Q or nonnegative measurable. (F3) v, Dv, G, DG are continuous, hence bounded on Q̄; every function below is a bounded measurable function on a set of finite measure, so all integrals are finite and Fubini applies.

1. Product rule. H := vG is C¹ with DH(x)h = (Dv(x)h)G(x) + v(x)DG(x)h. Hence ∂_iH_i = (∂_iv)G_i + v∂_iG_i and, by (F1), Σ_i ∂_iH_i(x) = Dv(x)(G(x)) + v(x) div G(x).

2. Divergence theorem on the box. For each i and x' ∈ Q', t ↦ H_i(ι_i(t, x')) is C¹ on [a, b] with derivative ∂_iH_i(ι_i(t, x')), so by the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt) ∫_a^b ∂_iH_i(ι_i(t, x')) dt = H_i(ι_i(b, x')) − H_i(ι_i(a, x')). Integrating over x' ∈ Q' and using (F2): ∫_Q ∂_iH_i = ∫_{Q'}[H_i(ι_i(b, x')) − H_i(ι_i(a, x'))] dx'. (Alternatively this is Mathlib MeasureTheory.integral_divergence_of_hasFDerivAt_off_countable on the box [a, b]^{Fin n}, transported through the measure-preserving identification Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ); that lemma lives in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.DivergenceTheorem, which is outside the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission and must then be added as an import. Adding Mathlib imports to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean is accepted practice in this run (29 accepted nodes do so, e.g. 10 import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense and 10 import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.SmoothApprox); the challenge and the solution of the child comparator both import the candidate Submission, so the frozen type is unaffected. The coordinatewise route of steps 2 and 4 needs only intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt, MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove and PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, all available under `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`.)

3. Summing over i with step 1: ∫_Q v div G = Σ_i ∫_{Q'}[H_i(ι_i(b, x')) − H_i(ι_i(a, x'))] dx' − ∫_Q Dv(x)(G(x)) dx. Since |H_i| ≤ |v||G| ≤ |v| and |Dv(x)(G(x))| ≤ ‖Dv(x)‖|G(x)| ≤ ‖Dv(x)‖: |∫_Q v div G| ≤ ∫_Q ‖Dv‖ + Σ_i Σ_{c ∈ {a, b}} ∫_{Q'}|v(ι_i(c, x'))| dx'.

4. Face (trace) estimate. Fix i, c ∈ {a, b} and x' ∈ Q'. For t ∈ [a, b], the fundamental theorem of calculus along the segment between c and t gives |v(ι_i(c, x'))| ≤ |v(ι_i(t, x'))| + ∫_a^b |∂_iv(ι_i(r, x'))| dr. Averaging over t ∈ [a, b] (divide by s > 0): |v(ι_i(c, x'))| ≤ s^{−1}∫_a^b |v(ι_i(t, x'))| dt + ∫_a^b |∂_iv(ι_i(r, x'))| dr. Integrating over x' ∈ Q' and using (F2): ∫_{Q'}|v(ι_i(c, x'))| dx' ≤ s^{−1}∫_Q|v| + ∫_Q|∂_iv| ≤ 2∫_Q|v| + ∫_Q‖Dv‖, because s ≥ 1/2 and |∂_iv(x)| = |Dv(x)e_i| ≤ ‖Dv(x)‖.

5. Conclusion. There are 2n pairs (i, c), so by steps 3 and 4: |∫_Q v div G| ≤ ∫_Q‖Dv‖ + 2n(2∫_Q|v| + ∫_Q‖Dv‖) = (2n + 1)∫_Q‖Dv‖ + 4n∫_Q|v|. With n = m + 1: (2(m + 1) + 1)∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv‖ + 4(m + 1)∫_{Q_δ}|v|. ∎
proof_key_steps: Product rule: div(vG) = Dv(G) + v div G, with div = Σ_i ∂_i(·)_i in the standard basis.
Divergence theorem on the box [δ, 1 − δ]ⁿ (FTC in each coordinate plus Fubini): ∫_{Q_δ}∂_i(vG_i) equals the difference of the two face integrals.
|∫ v div G| ≤ ∫‖Dv‖ + Σ over the 2n faces of ∫_face|v|.
Face estimate by FTC and averaging over a side of length s ≥ 1/2: ∫_face|v| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|v| + ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv‖.
Summing: (2n + 1)∫‖Dv‖ + 4n∫|v|.

subproblems.title: Trace estimate on the unit cube for functions of variation at most V tested on bounded C¹ fields

If w : ℝⁿ → ℝ is integrable on Q₁ and V ∈ ℝ satisfies ∫_{Q₁} w · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1, then for every C¹ map G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with |G(y)| ≤ 1 for all y: |∫_{Q₁} w · div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|w| (2n + 1 = 2(m + 1) + 1, 4n = 4(m + 1)).

Sibling results used. smooth_approx (dimred_mbl_dt_cbm_smooth_approx): for w integrable on Q₁ with hyp(w, V) and δ > 0 there are C¹ functions v_k with ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ ≤ V for all k and ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − w| → 0. smooth_trace (dimred_mbl_dt_cbm_smooth_trace): for C¹ v, C¹ G with |G| ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1/4, |∫_{Q_δ} v div G| ≤ (2n + 1)∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv‖ + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|v|.

Fix w integrable on Q₁ with hyp(w, V), and G C¹ with |G| ≤ 1.

0. Boundedness of div G. DG is continuous and A ↦ trace A is linear on the finite-dimensional space L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), so div G is continuous; it is therefore bounded on the compact set [0, 1]ⁿ ⊇ Q₁: |div G| ≤ M on Q₁ for some M ≥ 0. Hence w · div G is integrable on Q₁ and on every Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ (it is a.e.-strongly measurable and |w div G| ≤ M|w|).

1. Fix δ ∈ (0, 1/4] and take v_k from smooth_approx (δ > 0). Each v_k is continuous, hence bounded on the bounded set Q_δ; so v_k, v_k div G and v_k − w are integrable on Q_δ, and ε_k := ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − w| → 0. By smooth_trace (0 ≤ δ ≤ 1/4) and 2n + 1 > 0: |∫_{Q_δ} v_k div G| ≤ (2n + 1)∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|v_k| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|v_k|.

3. Limit δ ↓ 0. Let δ_j := 1/(j + 4) ∈ (0, 1/4], δ_j ↓ 0; every point of Q₁ lies in Q_{δ_j} for all large j. Dominated convergence as δ ↓ 0 gives the bound on Q₁.
